gap-blue-white-1962.palette: interpretive screen colors, not calibrated pigments
gap-blue-white-1962.notes: Actual primary gallery page explicitly captions the reproduced painting Blue White (1962), oil on canvas, Rose Art Museum. Two blue masses nearly meet at the center; white wedges open at top and bottom. Different from the adjacent small collage Study for Blue White. Whole rectangular painted support retained; photo margins omitted. Physical dimensions remain unknown.

gap-blue-white-2006.palette: interpretive screen colors, not calibrated pigments
gap-blue-white-2006.notes: Actual museum lobby photograph credited E. Scott McDonald and independent project architect Scott Lauer show the full work: blue upper panel joined to a white lower panel. The current exhibition hero depicts Youngerman May, not this work; it is excluded as a reference. This drawing retains the observed oblique projection, not an invented frontal parallelogram or dimensions. Museum describes the commission as a painting; its older wall-sculpture wording remains a classification note.

gap-ormesson-1950.palette: interpretive screen colors, not calibrated pigments
gap-ormesson-1950.notes: Actual color illustration: Else van Sterkenburg-Fransen, Radboud University bachelor thesis (2017), PDF 65 fig 25. Foundation EK 29 installation and MoMA 1973 note 26 independently identify the painting/date. Three white joined panels retain the separate black and green chimney-derived motifs. The thesis reports 83.8×224.2 cm, but those dimensions are kept as secondary evidence only, not promoted to measured primary facts. Observed reproduction aspect retained despite its difference from the secondary dimensional ratio. Panel contours approximated; texture omitted.

sfmoma-v3-99-348.palette: interpretive screen colors, not calibrated pigments
sfmoma-v3-99-348.notes: Schematic of the directly inspected museum color image: central pale pointed lens, dark central seam, smaller lower teardrop and pale angular underpainting on the complete rectangular canvas. Low-contrast tonal layers, brushwork, worn edges and faint blue traces are simplified. Pale screen colors are intentionally retained; this is a major-motif navigation study, not a facsimile.
